content.explanation: WebAssembly, often called WASM, was created to enable high-performance applications inside browsers. Some workloads such as games, video editing, CAD tools, machine learning, and scientific computing require more performance than JavaScript can efficiently provide. WebAssembly allows languages like C++, Rust, and others to compile into a compact binary format that browsers can execute quickly.
content.example: A browser-based video editor may use WebAssembly for heavy video processing.
content.analogy: Using a sports car for a race instead of a family car.
content.keyTakeaway: WebAssembly brings near-native performance to browsers.
